notes.hourly_co2_answer: Yes. EIA publishes estimated hourly CO2 emissions per BA (total, by fuel, imported/exported, and the CO2 intensity of generated and of consumed electricity, lb/kWh) beginning 2018-07-01, but NOT in the six-month BALANCE/INTERCHANGE CSVs. They are in the keyless per-BA workbooks https://www.eia.gov/electricity/gridmonitor/knownissues/xls/{BA}.xlsx (sheet 'Published Hourly Data', columns 'CO2 Factor: COL/NG/OIL', 'CO2 Emissions: COL/NG/OIL/Other', 'CO2 Emissions Generated/Imported/Exported/Consumed', 'Positive Generation', 'Consumed Electricity', 'CO2 Emissions Intensity for Generated/Consumed Electricity'). Method (EIA About page): BA-specific average CO2 factors from EIA-923 plant data and EPA factors, CHP excluded; consumption intensity via a multiregional input-output model over BA transfers. Published for yesterday by about 4 p.m. ET today. Downloaded here for 18 candidate BAs under ba_workbooks/.
notes.timestamp_convention: EIA labels each hour by its END ('UTC Time at End of Hour'; workbook Notes: 'Hour 1 corresponds to the time period 12:00 AM - 1:00 AM'). The tidy table data/interim/eia930/balance.parquet uses ts_utc = hour START (UTC end minus 1 h).
notes.publication_lags: EIA About page: demand ~1 h after the operating hour; net generation, generation by source and total interchange for yesterday by ~11:00 a.m. ET today; interchange with each neighbour for the day before yesterday by ~11:00 a.m. ET; the BA day-ahead demand forecast for each hour of TODAY by ~11:00 a.m. ET today (EIA-930 instructions: the daily file due 7:00 a.m. ET carries 'yesterday's hourly day-ahead demand forecast for today'); CO2 for yesterday by ~4:00 p.m. ET. Files are regenerated daily (server Last-Modified = retrieval day), so values can be revised; sha256 pins this snapshot.
notes.files_not_in_six_month_set: EIA930_Reference_Tables.xlsx (BA codes, names, time zones, generation-only flags, retirement dates) from https://www.eia.gov/electricity/930-content/EIA930_Reference_Tables.xlsx; ba_workbooks/*.xlsx as above.
